findings.title: The December 'expected >= grade 5' checkpoint is unreachable at any observed or plausible pace, and its only fallback is 'extend Phase 2'

Below that -> recommend extending Phase 2 before starting the Higher layer."
findings.problem: 39 of the 55 Foundation-tier (F or F/H) topics are not secure (12 developing, 12 gap, 15 not started). A mid-December mock is 14.4 weeks away, so every Foundation topic secure by then needs 2.7 topics/week reaching secure, and under the skill's own rules a topic needs at least two separate touches (teach, then a later independent check at >= 80%), i.e. about 5.4 topic-touches a week on top of starter slots for 8 ageing secures and 14 loose ends. Observed since the tracker opened on 19 Aug (16 days, 3 sessions on 2 days): 0 topics to secure, 2 to developing (P1, P2-P3), 1 demoted (A4) — net secure -1. The sample is tiny (three sessions) and says little about capacity, but it says nothing in favour of 2.7/week. The grade-5 bar itself is 186/240 = 77.5% on the stored June 2024 row, against 148/240 = 61.7% last time with Geometry, Probability and Statistics at 0 of 23 topics secure. The bullet also says '172/240 equivalent' while the service will convert against the stored June 2024 row, on which 172-185 is a grade 4 — so the appendix and the dashboard would disagree about whether the checkpoint was met. Below the bar the plan says only 'extend Phase 2': no date, no Foundation default, no deferral criterion.
findings.why_it_matters: A checkpoint set two grades above the evidenced level guarantees a December 'missed target' on a paper that would actually show real progress. For a 13-year-old with ADHD who is studying largely alone, that is the most demotivating message the system can send at the darkest point of the year. A checkpoint that can tell 'on course for 4', 'on course for 5' and 'behind' apart is also what the February tier decision actually needs.
findings.proposal: Replace bullet 1 with: "**Dec 2026 Foundation full mock** — three timed papers from one AQA series of June 2024 or later (the series whose boundaries are stored), sat within 7 days, logged as one attempt with blanks per paper. Expected: >= grade 4 on that series' own boundaries (June 2024: >= 157/240); stretch >= 172. Read it three ways. >= 186 (Foundation grade 5): she is at the Foundation ceiling — run the Feb Higher mock. 157-185: Foundation entry is the working assumption; the Feb Higher mock is optional evidence. < 157: Foundation entry, target 4 secure / 5 stretch, and put a June 2028 sitting on the table in the same report. Whatever the mark, report blanks per paper and marks lost per strand." Add a dated budget line under it: "Budget to 14 Dec: the 12 gap and 12 developing lower-tier topics secure (24 topics = 1.7/week); the 15 not-started lower-tier topics at least developing."
findings.evidence_needed: Proximal, attainable goals and self-efficacy (Bandura & Schunk 1981; Locke & Latham goal-setting) — attainability matters more for ADHD; plus the arithmetic in 'numbers' (N3, N5, N8).

findings.problem: G20 'Pythagoras and trigonometry' runs from Pythagoras to the sine and cosine rules in one ref; A9-A10 is secure with Higher-depth content untaught. If Higher were chosen, the post-December layer is not 9 topics but 9 Higher-only plus the Higher depth of 22 F/H topics — up to 31 topics of new work in the 22 weeks from 14 Dec to 14 May (1.4/week) on top of finishing Foundation. The tier decision would be taken on a topic table that cannot show this.
findings.why_it_matters: It is another reason the Higher intention is under-costed (finding 2). It also means a Higher mock in February will hit content that the table calls secure, which reads to the student as 'I thought I knew this'.
findings.proposal: If Foundation is chosen, change nothing in the data but add one sentence to the progress-report rules: 'secure on an F/H topic means Foundation depth unless the evidence says otherwise'. If Higher stays live after December, extend the subject with H-depth sub-refs (A18H quadratics by formula/completing the square, G20H sine and cosine rules, and so on) via tracker_create_subject, which adds topics without resetting statuses, so the Higher layer becomes countable.
findings.evidence_needed: AQA 8300 specification content markers (Higher-only content is indicated within each spec reference) — policy-document.

findings.title: Geometry, Probability and Statistics have zero secure topics: 23 of 55 Foundation topics and roughly a quarter to a third of Foundation marks
findings.where: /home/user/education-study-tracker/php/lib/seed.php lines 82-111 (G, P and S strands); /home/user/education-study-tracker/php/lib/mcp.php lines 919-921 (gaps ordered by tier string only); /root/.claude/skills/synced/4573a9f7-2a0f-468d-a55f-752a46b4cb7c_a7c9a5f9-6655-41a2-821b-3115c7ffaf84/gcse-progress-tracker/references/subjects/maths.md (no strand budget).
findings.problem: Lower-tier secure by strand: N 5/11, A 6/14 (after the A4 demotion), R 5/7, G 0/13, P 0/5, S 0/5. On AQA's published Foundation weightings (Geometry 12-18%, Probability and Statistics 12-18% — approximate, not re-verified this session) that is about 58-86 of the 240 marks sitting in strands with no secure topic, which is where the 38 marks between 148 and 186 have to come from. Probability (5 short topics, 2 now developing after 2 Sep) and S2/S4 are the highest marks-per-week topics on the sheet. The queue orders gaps by tier and then insertion order, not by mark yield.
findings.why_it_matters: Pace is not only topics per week but marks per topic-week. Choosing the next twelve topics by yield is the difference between a December mock that shows +30 marks and one that shows +10 for the same effort.
findings.proposal: Add a strand line to the December budget in maths.md: "By 14 Dec: P1-P8 secure (5 topics); S2 and S4 secure; G3, G9-G12 and G14-G16 secure; G17-G18 and G20 developing." Let the tutor skill's step 2 ('Teach... the top priority gap from the review queue') take the first unfinished item from that list. Optionally add a `weight` per strand on the subject row and sort gaps by it in mcp.php line 921.
findings.evidence_needed: AQA 8300 content weightings by tier (specification; policy-document).

findings.title: The countdown counts to a provisional date and to the wrong milestone
findings.where: /home/user/education-study-tracker/php/lib/dashboard.php lines 178-183 and 367-370 ('N days to the exam'); /home/user/education-study-tracker/php/lib/seed.php line 119 (exam_date 2027-05-14) and line 134 ('Paper 1 date provisional').
findings.problem: The nearest hard date for the plan is the tier and entry decision (about 21 Feb 2027, 170 days), before it the December mock (101 days); neither appears anywhere on the page, and the exam date it counts to is provisional. A single large red 252 is time pressure with no next step attached.
findings.why_it_matters: For a student with ADHD, a distant deadline is nearly invisible and a near one is actionable. The page should show the next thing, not only the last thing.
findings.proposal: Add an optional `next_checkpoint` (date and label) on the subject row (migration step, argument on tracker_create_subject) and render it as a second smaller badge above the exam countdown: '101 days to the December mock'. List the dated checkpoints from the appendix as a small table under the stats cards. Keep the exam countdown, and update exam_date when AQA's final June 2027 timetable is published.
findings.evidence_needed: Proximal deadlines and ADHD time horizon (Barkley; expert consensus).
